name: Backpropagation
strandNote: Optional for every quant role. For machine learning research roles, and for using and building AI tools with judgement.
description: Compute every gradient of a network by the chain rule on a graph, then write the autograd that trains it.

skills.bp-chain: The chain rule on a graph

levels.name: The chain rule on a graph

requires.why: The chain rule, product rule and standard derivatives give each node's local derivative.
Partial derivatives and the chain rule with two inputs, read off the graph.
The Value class builds on writing a small class with an initialiser and methods.
Topological order is retaught in one screen; the sort lesson there goes deeper.
Trains the network by the gradient descent and step-size choice taught there.
The curvature term shows why a central difference's error shrinks like the step squared.
Gradient checks compare floats by relative error, never by equality.
One neuron by hand, and why XOR needs a hidden layer, met in Stage 0.
Arrays, sums along an axis and broadcasting, whose gradient is a sum.
Matrix products, transposes and NumPy matrices for the backward pass of a product.
Softmax with cross-entropy is the loss that info level 2 defines.

lessonNames.l14-broadcasting-backwards: Broadcasting runs backwards as a sum

lessonObjectives.l1-expression-as-graph: Draw an expression as a graph of operations and compute its forward values.
lessonObjectives.l2-local-derivatives: Compute the derivative of each operation's output with respect to each of its inputs.
lessonObjectives.l3-multiplying-along-a-path: Find the gradient of the output with respect to an input by multiplying local derivatives along the path.
lessonObjectives.l4-every-gradient-by-hand: Derive every gradient of a small expression by hand, working back from the output.
lessonObjectives.l5-where-paths-meet: Add the contributions of every path when a value is used more than once.
lessonObjectives.l6-doing-the-work-in-order: Order a graph's nodes topologically and run the backward pass in the reverse order.
lessonObjectives.l7-a-number-that-remembers: Write a `Value` class that records how each number was made, with addition and multiplication.
lessonObjectives.l8-backward-in-code: Implement `backward()` for the `Value` class and match the gradients worked by hand.
lessonObjectives.l9-neuron-of-values: Build a tanh neuron from `Value` operations and backpropagate through it.
lessonObjectives.l10-layers-and-networks: Build a layer and a multilayer perceptron from neurons, and count its parameters.
lessonObjectives.l11-the-training-loop: Train a small network by gradient descent: forward, zero the gradients, backward, step.
lessonObjectives.l12-checking-gradients: Check backpropagated gradients against central differences, and choose the step that makes the check trustworthy.
lessonObjectives.l13-backward-through-a-product: Derive the gradients of a matrix product from the scalar case, and check their shapes.
lessonObjectives.l14-broadcasting-backwards: Sum a gradient over the broadcast axes so that it has the shape of its input.
lessonObjectives.l15-softmax-cross-entropy: Derive the gradient of softmax with cross-entropy as the probabilities minus the one-hot target.
lessonObjectives.l16-a-small-array-autograd: Build an array autograd in NumPy and check it against central differences to relative error $10^{-6}$ in float64.
